Two or more: align to the selection. One: align to the canvas centre. A group counts as one thing.
draw order
Signals draw in list order — later is in front. A move keeps the selection's own relative order.
arrange to grid
Every shape on the page onto one grid, one cell each, in z-order. Each is scaled uniformly to fill its cell and centred in it, so nothing is stretched and no shape is resampled; a group counts as one unit. Cell size 0 is auto — taken from the largest shape on the page. One undo puts the page back.
morph
Two shapes are N samples of the same parameter circle, so the space between them is a lerp of two arrays — every intermediate is a real closed curve and there is no way to make a kink. Select two for a strip, four for a bilinear grid over the corners.

mirror lock
While it is on, sculpting a leaf moves its reflection the mirrored way. The axis is the shape's own centre and is drawn on the canvas. Partners are matched by position at the moment the drag starts, so a shape that is already symmetric stays symmetric.

lab
The edit view (double-click a shape to open it, leaves, the straighten/smooth pair) and the lab pane (the instruments — what they measure, not what you are making). Both off by default, so the plain page is the drawing. Turning them on reloads the page with ?--lab=1 ; your work is saved and comes straight back.
Observation instruments, not drawing tools. Each changes how the shape is measured or reported — none change the geometry. Safe to sweep.
scatter
A crowd for the instruments to measure, and a load to measure them under. Primitives spread at random over the whole canvas — random position, size, turn and colour — dropped into the scene you already have, then the view opens up 15% so the field has a margin. Every one lands at the same 256-leaf floor as any other new shape: the crowd used to arrive at 64, which made the leaf count on a mixed page mean nothing. The cost of that is real and the count selector is where you pay it — 100 shapes runs at about 16 ms a frame, 250 at 55. The status line reports the totals and the cost of one frame. Press it again to stack another batch; one undo takes each scatter back.
one-bit rings
The Acquisitive Observer's bottom rung: every placed mark's ray ring runs at C = 2 — a single held bit, the cell a half-turn. The winding survives to the last rung (a ring cannot rail, even one bit wide), and silence becomes the default: a mark the sweep does not enclose is dead silent — zero cells over the whole sweep, not a cancelling wobble — unless the journey genuinely wound and unwound, which reads as net 0 with its turns named. The area atom runs at one bit too, where quantization performs the calibration: κ = 0 and the raw sum is the Magnus integer — at this rung only. The instrument constant is the instrument's, not the world's, and it moves: 0.0022 for this editor's keyhole letters at C = 64, 0.1604 and 0.1870 for the paper's two Python realizations, with the corrected class readings identical across all of them (The Fourth Atom §3). And the audit line under the word is worth exactly what §2.1 scoped it to: the discrete shuffle is exact in whatever streams it is handed, so it certifies this register's arithmetic and never its reading. And the letter-maker spells the sweep: each full turn around a mark is two cells, an accumulator per ring emits a letter at ±C, and the word appears under the class line — segmentation dissolved by coarseness.
the contact walker
The Contact Observer's instrument, in this world: the shapes become solid , and a walker is released whose steps the world may refuse — the refusal is one bit, and the only arrival. It flies ballistically, hugs on contact (wall on left), and certifies a lap only by the four clauses: a full turn of its own chords, odometer closure, contact in the loop, and the touches themselves going round (the surround form — no half-plane holds them). Certified laps become tags in the odometer's frame; tags that land inside the guard band merge — that count is b₀, read by dead reckoning and nothing smaller. Each tag carries the winding of its lap, ±1 — the b₁ column. A failed hug climbs the curl ladder: smaller steps, the rung the failure chose. The ledger draws at the top left; the walk, its touches and its tags draw on the canvas. Geometry is frozen at release — recall and release again after editing.
THE PIVOT. Wind in, certify, unwind out — the maze journey is a recursion , and the corner is its test. On the way down every look pays: the register speaks, symbols fire, complexity is being entered. The base case is the corner — the register falls silent, the road holds the free symbol, the lap closes at 2π — and that silence is the only signal that there is nothing deeper: the walker does not choose to turn back, it reads the turn on its own meter. Then the return: the wound turns pop like stack frames — 36 full laps cancel on one seed, 244 on another — and the value handed back at the top is the class, π, the antipode of home. Deeper or shallower is never a decision; it is the corner's verdict, look by look: sentence off the corner — descend; sentence at the corner — certify and return. The same cell prices the base rule's spend, balances the Cauchy lens, opens the maze's door and pivots its recursion. One corner, four duties, no coincidence.
shape sheet
Every primitive in the library, once, on a grid — the catalogue at the working rung instead of at twenty-eight pixels in the popover, where a spoon and a magnifier look alike. It is also a fixture: one press gives every kind of contour the pipeline handles (smooth, cornered, holed) in one reproducible scene, which is a better thing to point an instrument at than a circle. It replaces the page; one undo brings the old one back.
leaf-colour tests
The five leaf paints, each against the whole corpus . One shape at a time a colouring is decoration; sixty-four shapes side by side under the same colouring it is a measurement — the differences between the shapes are the content of the picture. The shapes are identical in all five sheets and only the paint changes, so the sheets compare to each other as well as internally: the convexity the bearing sheet reads off its entry count is invisible on the position sheet, and knowing which instrument sees what is the point. Built at N = 64 — the largest leaf count that still resolves into individual dots in one cell — with the contour dimmed and the fisheye off, so the census in each caption is the census on the page. Replaces the current page in one history frame.
two-atom tests
The Two-Atom Observer's checks, on this library. Each representable primitive is swept by both atoms : the radial floor rule, whose checksum Σ(i−c) must read 0 on a closed contour, and the angular atom — a direction held on a ring of 64 cells , whose cells must sum to exactly one circumference (winding 1, an integer by format). Reported per shape: both checksums, each register's bits per look, and the largest single cell count — a ring cannot rail, so a sharp corner arrives as one big count and costs nothing. The two economies run in opposite directions: the radial register charges for corners, the angular for roundness — the circle's angular spend H(64/512) = 0.544 is the convex ceiling : concentrated turning (corners) is cheaper, and concave features (petals, teeth) pay beyond it for their reversals. Laid out like the frequency ladder : every qualifying primitive drawn in its own cell with its key results under it, and the verdict carried by the contour's colour — teal where the checksum is 0 and the winding lands exactly on one circumference, gold within tolerance, red where it misses. The aggregate is in the status line. This one replaces the page, in a single history frame: one undo brings your work back.
three-atom tests
The Three-Atom Observer's library run, with The Acquisitive Observer's one-bit column riding along. Each representable primitive is placed about the first mark (its own centroid); a second mark sits at distance 2.5 in shape units — the corpus separation. Three atoms read the sweep: the radial floor rule (checksum 0, the closing arrival handed), and one ring per mark on the bearing of that mark — rays read residues; chords read Hopf. The windings must be integer-exact — (1, 0), the homology class — at C = 64 and again at C = 2 , where the ring is a single held bit and every mark the sweep does not enclose should be dead silent: zero cells, not zero net. The prediction under test: ring 1 costs H(64/512) = 0.544 on every shape alike — the ray ring has no shape term — while ring 2 pays only the spectator's subtense, dearest for the shapes with the widest silhouettes. Laid out like the frequency ladder : every qualifying primitive drawn in its own cell with its key results under it, and the verdict carried by the contour's colour — teal where the triple is exact and the one-bit ring is too, gold where only the C = 64 triple holds, red where it fails. The aggregate is in the status line. This one replaces the page, in a single history frame: one undo brings your work back.
recovery tests
How many observers does a shape cost ? Every other run asks what one observer reads; this one asks how many of them it takes to get the shape back — and the answer turns out to be a measurement of the shape, which no single ring can make: the ray ring has no shape term (§3), billing 0.544 on a circle and a star alike. A ring at a standpoint reads one integer, the winding about that point; the integer is locally constant and jumps by ±1 across the contour , so the curve is the discontinuity set of a field every observer in it is blind to. Four standpoints are read, and a cell is split only where its corners disagree — the disagreement is the curve, a test the instrument runs on its own readings with no distance, crossing or normal computed anywhere. The straddling cells at scale ε are a covering, so N(ε)·ε is the arc length and the log–log slope is the box-counting dimension ; both are reported, and the length is checked against the polyline's own — a number the rings never see. Refinement halts at δ* = (s/2)·tan(π/2C) , the near-miss radius: closer than that, one look can carry the bearing past τ* and the ring lies in confident integers. The recovery has a horizon, and the instrument names it in advance. Laid out like the frequency ladder : every qualifying primitive drawn in its own cell with its key results under it, and the verdict carried by the contour's colour — teal where the recovered length lands within 5% of the contour's own, gold where it lands inside the gauge band [0.785, 1.111] that no single-lattice census could escape even in the continuum, red outside it. The aggregate is in the status line. This one replaces the page, in a single history frame: one undo brings your work back.
cauchy tests
The forced measure meets the floor rule. Each representable primitive is read radially by the base rule (the same census and sweep as the base-rule tests), then both the true and the held radii are mapped through the Cauchy lens — v → 2h₀·(2/π)·atan(v/h₀), h₀ the shape's median radius (the order-native unit; the mean is not invited). The lens is Lipschitz in log -radius with constant 2h₀/π, peaked at the corner v = h₀ — so the register's uniform half-step log band must become a bounded view-space error ≤ h₀·σ/π , largest at the corner, vanishing at home and horizon. The prediction under test: every in-band ratio ≤ 1, the peak sitting near ρ = 1 — the base rule and the Cauchy chart are conjugate : equal cells in log are exactly the cells a fisheye spends at its own balance. The far tail rides along: the fraction of each contour beyond the corner, and the subtense discount the lens grants it. The corner here is the same cell that pivots the walker's maze: the lens balances exactly where the recursion turns. A report, not a scene.
opening the shapes
The fisheye opens a closed shape, with the situated reader at the middle of the opening. Each single-outline primitive is laid evenly along its outline and read from its area centre: h = |x − cx|, v = |y − cy|, the reading v/h. Four numbers say how it opens: the corner (the share of the outline read before v/h = 1), the middle (the median v/h), the tail (40 × the share beyond v/h = 40) and the head (40 × the share below v/h = 1/40). The circle gives ½, 1, 2/π, 2/π. b is the breadth ratio, max v / max h. The last line under each shape gives the same four for an ellipse of the same b , laid the same way. The contour's colour is how far the shape's corner and middle sit from that ellipse's — teal within 0.02, gold within 0.1, red beyond — a distance, not a verdict. Laid evenly by direction instead, every shape opens as the circle does; that control is in the status line. This one replaces the page, in a single history frame: one undo brings your work back.
near and far
A flat outline that glows evenly, read from a point on its axis at distance d through its area centre. The light arriving, as a share of its most, is the glowing disc's law s²/(1 + s²) averaged round the outline, with s = R(θ)/d for the outline's reach R(θ) in each direction: one reading per direction, as opening the shapes reads them. Far off it goes as the inverse square of d, set by the outline's area (the mean of R²); close in, its shortfall goes as d², set by the outline's harmonic reach (the mean of 1/R²). The two ends see two sizes. For the circle they are one size, and the near law is the far law read through the flip, f(1/s) = 1 − f(s), exactly, the middle at d = R. Under each shape: Q , the mean of R² times the mean of 1/R² (1 only for the circle); the middle d½, where half the light has arrived; the corner the two ends would set, D  = (mean R² / mean 1/R²) ¼ ; and the flip , the largest departure from f(1/s) = 1 − f(s) taken about the middle. Teal : the flip holds to 10⁻³ and the middle sits at D within 2%: one corner. Gold : the flip holds to 0.02. Red : the two ends set two corners. Shapes whose centre lies outside the outline, or whose outline crosses itself, are left out. Replaces the current page in one history frame.
the shape, octave by octave
SPN §3.3: as octaves are added, the shape emerges . Each single-outline primitive is laid evenly along its outline and read from its area centre as v/h, as in opening the shapes . Each reading is kept as its side of the corner, its octave counted outward from the corner (by the share: v/h before it, h/v past it) and its place t within that octave, in sixteen steps; past the twelfth octave the readings are lumped. The shape's readings are set against the circle's, and the difference is spread over the octaves. Under each shape: how much of its difference from the circle is seen once octaves 0, 2 and 4 are read (both sides); and how much octave 0, the reader's own, carries a reading (its share of the difference over its share of the circle's readings, 0.41). Teal : octave 0 carries under 0.8 per reading, the shape shows itself away from the corner, as the claim says. Gold : 0.8 to 1, or the shape reads exactly as the circle (its difference is only in the magnitudes). Red : octave 0 carries more than its share; this shape shows itself most near the corner. Replaces the current page in one history frame.
the corner reads the breadth
SPN §2.2 (R142), and RaP §8 and T8. A shape whose v breadth is b times its h breadth, laid as the circle is, has the share of its readings before the corner, v = h, set by b; in an evenly spread world that share is the sweep's share up to 1/b, so a reader can read b back from where its corner falls among its arrivals. Each primitive is stretched in v by b = 1.5, 2, 3, 5 and 10, and b is read back three ways. Even share : laid along the unstretched outline, then stretched (the lay the circle uses), read with the evenly spread world's rule. Shape known : the same arrivals, read against the shape's own unstretched readings (situation 2 inside). Along the stretched outline : laid evenly along the outline after stretching, read with the evenly spread world's rule. Laid evenly by direction instead, the share is exactly ½ for every shape and every b, and the corner reads nothing. Under each shape, the median error in b over the five stretches. Teal : the even-share reading is within 5%; gold within 20%; red beyond: the corner reads b only against this shape, not against the evenly spread world. A shape whose breadths already differ before it is stretched (the ellipse, the tall oval) is read for its whole breadth ratio, stretch included, so it shows red by construction; the known line, read against the shape itself, is the one that isolates the stretch. The rule's step from the share back to b uses arctan, the shortcut (R148). Replaces the current page in one history frame.
depth of a shape
R180, "this is depth. its the recursion" , under R183 (h is the reader). A reader stands on each outline, where it is nearest the shape's unit circle (its mean radius about its centroid), and reads one facing: home is its own neighbourhood along its tangent, the corner a quarter turn on, the mathematical horizon the point straight across. The bare circle read this way is the evenly spread world — v/h = tan(θ/2), the fisheye — and holds no depth. What depth holds is the shape's departure from that circle, address by address: the reader's own sweep at 16 leaves, then every octave entered as another whole sweep holding what the levels above did not, to level 3. Teal : held to 5% of the departure by level 1; gold : by level 3; red : not by level 3; grey: not scored (no standpoint on its unit circle, or the facing folds). Plan, predictions and results: wander/plans/shp-plan.md §6. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the nested fisheye
Every octave is the 0 to π/2 sweep, and the fisheye is the sweep: "perfect clarity at home, gently compression until the corner and aggressive accelerationg compression after the corner." This shows how a child's sweep lies inside its parent's reading. The child's leaves, evenly spaced in its own turn and generated from its corner, are counted in eight equal stretches of the parent's doubling, read v/h below the reader's corner and h/v above it. Seen from the parent, each half of the child is exactly proportional — R183's front [0,1] and back [0,1] once more — so its clarity is full at its home, ½ at its corner, and full again at its mathematical horizon wall. The past-the-corner compression is the back half read the other way. Every child lies the same way, at every level ( teal : as NST run 2 recorded). Plan: wander/plans/labs-plan.md . Replaces the page in one history frame.
walls
An entered octave presents what it holds inside its own octave and nothing outside, so where its detail is not zero at a wall the presented surface steps there: one side has been entered and the other has not. Two things, held level by level through one chain: ψ, detail on every wall, and χ, a thing that itself steps at every wall. At level 2, at the far wall (shared with the next child) and the near wall (the parent's own corner), with one side entered ( gold : a seam is expected) and then both ( teal : the seam closed to under half). Each cell is the presented surface across a narrow stretch either side of the wall. At the parent's corner the two children are each other's flip, so detail the flip leaves unchanged cancels in the step and detail it negates adds. Reproduces WNZ, WN2 and JMP; plan: wander/plans/labs-plan.md . Replaces the page in one history frame.
learning a shape from its encounters
Tom, 5 October: the advantage of full shape is that you know the answer, you compare the known shape with what the reader learns about it. The reader has its own h, nothing about the shape, and v is withheld: the shape sits D = 8, 16, 32 or 64 h's ahead, and for each of its directions that meets the outline the reader learns only where along that direction the meeting falls, as a count of its own h's held in one of 1,024 depth addresses: one sweep (1,024 leaves of the theorem), or nested (16 octaves of 64 leaves, each octave its own sweep, walls held at their own address). Five pathological shapes, generated here from their formulas (wander/patho). In each cell the true outline (verdict colour) carries the two learned outlines: blue the nested reader's, pink the one sweep's. Predicted first (SIT, 5 Oct): the nested reader's depth error stays flat with distance (kill if not); the one sweep's grows; near home the one sweep is finer. Python run: nested 0.7% at every distance; one sweep ×23 from 4 to 128 h. Teal : nested holds better. Gold : one sweep holds better (expected within about two octaves). Red : the nested reader's error is over 1%. Replaces the current page in one history frame.
what a reader cannot see
A point of the outline is seen if the reader's ray towards it meets the outline there first. Outside : the shape 32 h ahead, turned to 16 orientations (made from the theorem's leaves, no trigonometry), and what is seen pooled over the turns. Inside : the reader at the shape's area centre, where that lies in the hollow. Curled and spiral shapes from the pathological library (wander/patho), with an ellipse and a lobed shape as controls. Predicted first (OCC, INS, 5 Oct): the share seen from one view falls as the shape curls or winds; turning recovers open shapes; an inside standpoint recovers every curl (I1). Python run: curled 290° and 310° reach 82% and 63% from outside, 100% with the inside; spirals past a full turn stay hidden from both (92%, 72%, 66%). Tom's split of 22 September in shape terms: the outside reader sees the outside, and the inside has to be received from inside. Teal : seen whole from outside. Gold : whole only with the inside. Red : hidden from both. Replaces the current page in one history frame.
readers within readers
Three interactive sheets on one rule: a child reader stands where its parent saw furthest , taken from the parent's own record, up to three children a parent; a part of the outline or signal is coloured by the level of the reader that first sees it. Meeting distances are exact, so these show where standpoints must be, not how depth is held (that is SIT). READERS WITHIN READERS: spirals, curls and the strange tier, from 16 readers outside or one reader you place. From outside the levels step down each channel one stretch at a time (spiral5: level 6; hilbert: 7), and the same number of readers placed without nesting stays where the outside readers left it. From inside, the chain works out to the mouth and no further. THE STRANGE TIER: eight outlines with many hidden sides, every pocket open, no corners; levels count how many times the way in turns out of sight, not how complicated the outline is. SIGNALS AS LANDSCAPES: a signal read from h above the line, as in Recovering the Bump; the recursion runs along it as a relay, about one level per crest that hides, and the hand-offs follow the crest spacing. wander/patho: NST.md, STR.md, SIG.md. Overlays: nothing on the page is touched, except the strange tier's "put them on the page".
depth in TVF
TVF was built for breadth; it holds depth with no new syntax (THE DEPTH GUIDE): one sweep per document, TVF 16 1 1 , #meta address:@ for the reader's own sweep and @k.k… for each octave entered, concatenated; the root carries #meta reader: , the standpoint and frame. What each sweep holds is DPT's: the shape's departure from the reader's unit circle, the residual its levels above left, inside its own octave. THE TEST: every shape DPT scores is read to level 3, written as a depth file, read back , and scored against the known shape; and compared with breadth alone , one sweep holding as many values as the depth file. Teal : the file kept the reading (under 1e-6 of the departure) and depth beat breadth at the same count. Gold : kept, breadth as good or better. Red : the file changed the reading. SAVE writes the selected shape's depth file (DPT's standpoint on it); LOAD draws what the reader holds over the page, levels 0–3, blue to gold. wander/tvf-depth-test.md.
the sheets
Three interactive readings, each answering one question the corpus asks and none of them building anything. THE CLOSURE SHEET takes a shape's leaves as a closed sweep and reads every disagreement from a standpoint you drag: the radial half multiplies around the loop to exactly 1 wherever you stand, the angular half sums to a whole number of turns and jumps by one when you cross the contour — same disagreement, two accumulations, and only one of them obliged to come home . (The signature has moved out of this box and onto the page — see the signature below, which lays it out as ordinary shapes you can zoom, export and undo.) THE CYCLE SHEET takes several parties related pairwise in their own terms and asks whether one ground could serve them all: it can exactly when every cycle closes, and what is left over is an obstruction no third thing could have carried . All three are overlays — nothing on the page is touched, and there is nothing to undo. Escape closes them.
the signature
A figure described with nothing but disagreements, laid out on the page. Four points and four cross products give one number — the cross ratio of four rays, which is all the relation has and needs no coordinate, no unit and no frame — and taken along a contour they give a curve that identifies the figure . Every representable primitive is drawn three times in its own row of the page: as the page holds it, then restated by a projective account — a change of view, which moves every distance in it — and then its signature, drawn twice, before and after, one curve over the other. The second is not visible, because it is underneath the first. What the cells report is the pair of numbers that matters: how far the account moved the figure, and how far it moved the description. This one replaces the page in a single history frame , so one undo brings your work back, and everything on it is an ordinary shape — zoom it, export it, keep it.
closure tests
The two sheets' claims, run against this library rather than a picture. Every representable primitive is read as a closed sweep from two standpoints — its own centroid, and a point well outside it — and between successive leaves sits one disagreement D. Its two halves are accumulated separately. The radial half must multiply to exactly 1 at both standpoints: the reading closes, whatever the standpoint, because ratios of one quantity have nowhere else to go — the anchor's product-1 written around a whole sweep. The angular half must sum to 2π times an integer , and to a different integer at the two standpoints — the winding falls by one full turn when the standpoint leaves the contour. And Σ D is twice the signed area , which must not move when the standpoint does. Same D, two accumulations, and only one of them is obliged to come home: that is the facing's independence, measured on every shape here rather than argued. The cycle arithmetic rides along in the status line, on synthetic networks: readings built from a ground close every cycle to 1; a uniform twist of 0.12 leaves exactly 0.12 in any triangle, whatever the ground; and an intransitive ring is explained by no ground at all. A report, not a scene — nothing on the page is touched and there is nothing to undo.
facing tests
A refutation attempt, run against this library. The papers claim the facing is a second account and not a summary of the first — that no reading recovers it. If that is wrong, a constituent dies and six becomes five, so the claim is attacked here rather than defended. Two attacks. The first is exact : every primitive is read from its centroid, then mirrored and read again. Mirroring preserves every distance and negates every disagreement, so the radial stream must come back bit-identical while the facing comes back negated — a collision, not a constructed counterexample, and one per shape in the corpus. The second is statistical : from twelve standpoints per shape, scale-free features of the reading stream alone (its spread, its reversals, its spectrum) are used to predict the facing by nearest neighbour, with the shape itself excluded so nothing can be recognised rather than inferred. Direction should sit at chance. Enclosure — whether the sweep went round the standpoint at all — is the honest question: a reading stream does carry some of that, and how much is reported rather than assumed. A report, not a scene — nothing on the page is touched.
record tests
The record paper's claims, run rather than argued. Each primitive is read radially as a serial stream and a minimal reader writes it down: silence where the arrival stands within one grain of the held value, a signed tick per rung crossed, and ⊙ where the reading crosses equality. The string carries no magnitudes, no coordinates and no timestamps — order only. Four claims are tested. Scale-invariance : the whole history is rescaled by λ from 0.37 to 100 and the string must come back character for character the same, since a reading contains no factor an account could scale. The mark is every reader's mark : the same history read at three grains must place ⊙ at the identical arrivals — equality is a sign and a sign has no grain. Sufficiency : the rung address of every arrival is reconstructed from the string alone and must land within half a rung of the truth. Transfer with nothing exchanged : two readers of different grain recover the ratio of their grains by counting each other's ticks between marks they both kept for free, with no unit ever communicated. And the self-correction claim rides along — an arrival is deliberately dropped, the tick address drifts, and the marks must still align, because ⊙ does not lean on the count. A report, not a scene.
geometry tests
What geometry is available from the disagreement and the anchor alone — asked by taking it away. Fourteen points are read off each primitive, and the whole configuration is restated by three different accounts: a similarity (turn, scale, shift), a general affine map, and a projective one. Two things are then compared against the original. The chirotope — the sign of D on every triple, the relation's own data, no magnitude anywhere — and the cross ratio of four rays from a standpoint, which is built from four disagreements and nothing else: no length, no angle, no unit. Against them, distance ratios are carried along as a control. The prediction is sharp: the signs and the cross ratio come through every account unchanged while the distance ratios do not, and the harmonic set — the corner's own configuration — still reads exactly −1 after a map that has moved every distance in the figure. A mirror flips every sign at once, which is the facing again. If this holds, the geometry the pair owns is projective : incidence, order, and the cross ratio are the relation's; length and angle are the ground's. A report, not a scene.
number tests
Where the numbers come from. Everything here is built with joins and meets — draw the line through two points, take the point where two lines cross — and nothing else: no length is measured, no angle is taken, no unit is supplied, and the only decision ever made is the one the disagreement makes for free. Three stations are marked on a line and the complete quadrangle is used to construct the fourth harmonic of any three. That single construction is then run repeatedly. Taking the conjugate of n−1 against n and the far station steps the ladder, and its rungs come out as the integers . Taking the conjugate against the near and far stations gives negation . Taking it against the unit and its negative gives the reciprocal . Successor, negation, and inverse are the whole of rational arithmetic, so the field of the line is not assumed and then coordinatised — it is generated , by incidence alone. The last check is the one that matters: the whole figure is restated by a projective account and every construction run again, and the constructed points must be the images of the constructed points. What a pair builds this way it does not owe to any page. A report, not a scene.
reference tests
Where a serial reader gets the equality it marks against. The record paper marked crossings of the sweep's median reading — which requires every arrival to be held at once, and is therefore a parallel reference smuggled into a serial account. Three policies are compared here, from most parallel to most serial: the median , the first arrival kept and never updated (one slot beyond the held value), and the reader's own held value (one slot, nothing extra). Each is asked the two questions that make a mark worth having — does it survive the account rescaling the whole history, and do readers of different grain mark the same arrivals ? The answer separates them sharply, and it prices the mark. The residual fragility is reported too: a mark is a crossing , and where the sweep merely touches the reference without passing through it there is no crossing to find — which is what the symmetric primitives do, at exactly their symmetry points. A report, not a scene.
the disagreement, drawn
The corpus's seed is V A ·H B − V B ·H A — and that is twice the signed area of the triangle the reader's own standpoint makes with two arrivals . So the quantity everything here is built on has a picture: the room between two arrivals, seen from where the reader stands . These cells bring the second arrival round towards the first; as the triangle flattens the seed goes to nothing, and a quantity resting on it falls apart. That is the whole of the separation rule — why four readings must be far apart, why shared landmarks must be spread, and why the arithmetic fails on a difference of two nearly equal things. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the library, as it comes home
Eight figures from the library in pairs: on the left what was sent, on the right what a reader gathers back . The reaches sent run from 0.00 to 1.16 — a circle, a clover, a wedge, a spoon, a figure that grazes the reader — and every recovery comes home at reach one . The reader forms a ratio of the two extents and the reach cancels, so the shape is gone before the census ever sees it. What returns is not a poor reconstruction: it is the only figure the readings still permit . The shape was in the reach, and the reach is the coordinate nobody is issued. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the figure, by how many read it
The reader count walked from one to ninety-six in fives . A chain of m readers makes m −2 triples, each taking one stretch and rebuilding it in its own account, adjacent triples sharing two readers and no arrangement. So a larger swarm does not see more — it sees the same figure cut into more pieces . Below three readers there is no triple at all. Above that the figure comes back, and keeps coming back: the share each reader gets falls from three hundred arrangements to twelve across this page without the assembly minding . The swarm scales — which was not the expected answer. Starvation lies further out, where a stretch falls under the seven arrangements a triple needs to fix its own account. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the figure the ratio never carried
A reading is a ratio of the arrangement's two extents. Met at turn a with reach r , those extents are r·cos a and r·sin a — so the ratio is tan a and the reach cancels . These six figures could hardly differ more, one swinging elevenfold and one almost touching the reader, and every one sends ratio readings with the circle's own shape statistic . The ratio stream is a fact about the sweep , not about the figure. That is why a heart comes back as a unit circle: not because the recovery is poor, but because the ratio coordinate never carried the shape — the shape is in the reach, and the reach is the coordinate nobody was issued. Replaces the page in one history frame.
where the geometry goes
The companion to rung by rung : that page shows the shapes, this one shows what is happening underneath them. Read the disagreement line down the cells — it does not fade as the step coarsens, it holds near a third of the swing and then falls off a cliff to nothing . At the last cell every reading is at rung zero, and rung zero is the ratio one ; readings that are all one disagree about nothing. So the invariant computed on the reader's own corner is worthless long before the figure looks bad. The corner does not go fuzzy at a coarse step — it goes everywhere , and every arrangement at the corner is the same as none anywhere in particular. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the figure, rung by rung
A level of detail is not a setting — it is the register's step. Every reading is a ratio held to the nearest rung, so at a coarse enough step every reading is rung zero; and rung zero is the ratio one , which is a circle. That is the first cell, and it is not a failure: the unit curve is what a coarse enough register says about everything. Refine the step and the figure separates from the circle one rung at a time. The reader's own step is the second-to-last cell. Replaces the page in one history frame.
where the detail turns
The level of detail read as a relation: the register's step against the figure's swing , and the reading is the rung span , swing ÷ step. At home the figure fits inside one step and the reader holds its own laid unit all the way round — the unit curve, a statement about the reader . Toward the horizon the step dwindles and the figure arrives, never finishing. Between them is a corner: before it the record is in terms of the observer, after it in terms of the shape , counted in the observer's steps. It sits where the figure's largest departure from home equals half a step — and home is wherever the first look laid the unit, so the corner falls at a rung span of 1/(1+|u|): one when the unit is laid mid-swing, a half at an extreme. Cross it walks one register from home outward; move home holds the step and lays the unit in eleven places; ride a lobe is the registration that failed — a small feature on a larger one is not lost below its own corner, it is spoken in the larger feature's terms. A corner of the step-against-swing relation, not of V:H. Each replaces the page in one history frame.
the swarm, and the one that lied
Five parties, six readers, a figure none of them ever holds . Each reads its own stretch and a set of public landmarks every party reads . The seams are pinned by two shared readers — free, unaffected by the grain, and certifying nothing : the parts fuse without complaint even with a false one among them. What catches it is the landmarks, the only place two parties say something about the same thing. Each computes there a quantity no account can move, in its own account, and compares. The liar disagrees with everyone; the honest disagree with no one — so the swarm does not merely notice, it names . Replaces the page in one history frame.
the shape, assembled
A figure cut into four stretches, each read by its own triple of readers and rebuilt in that triple's own account — which is why the parts come out looking nothing like each other and nothing like the figure. Adjacent triples share two readers and no arrangement at all : the stretches do not overlap, and no reader ever sees an arrangement twice. Two shared readers pin two accounts to each other exactly, so the parts fuse, and the quantity every account agrees on comes back to the figure's own value. Nobody ever held the whole. What was shared was not a piece of the shape but a pair of readers. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the straight edge
The front-end result turned into an instrument : not does the quantity survive this front end , but certify, from readings alone, how far an unknown front end is from linear-fractional . The reference is a construction, not a unit — take any starting arrangement and step it by the same ratio three times, the register's own move; four marks laid down that way carry a cross ratio known by construction , at any scale and any position. Read them through the instrument, form the quantity from the snapped readings, and the signed departure from the constructed value is the instrument's bend. The grain jitters that departure but does not bias it, so the median of the signed departures over a sweep of the working range cancels the grain and keeps the bend — a gain, a bridge and a perspective all come back under a tenth of a percent, while a power law is caught from an exponent of 1.02 and the score grades with the bend. Two honest limits, both on the page: straight means linear-fractional, not unchanged — the bridge deforms every reading and is certified straight — and the certificate speaks only for the range that was probed . Replaces the page in one history frame.
the uncharacterised front end
What the reader's geometry is for . One figure is read through instruments nobody measured — an unknown gain, a ratiometric bridge , a pinhole's view along a line , an amplifier out of headroom — and the same four-reading quantity is formed from each. The drawn shapes come out wildly different; the quantity does not, so long as the front end is linear-fractional , which a bridge, a feedback amplifier and a perspective all are. An instrument that saturates is not, and it breaks. And the quantity needs the four readings far apart in the register : four readings within a rung of each other cannot carry it through any front end — which the reader can tell from its own symbols alone, so where it cannot answer it declines rather than guesses . Nothing here is calibrated, no reference is supplied, and no unit is issued. Replaces the page in one history frame.
what a hinge hides
The one exception to the recovery, laid out. A figure recovered from its arc element is the only smooth figure in front of the reader with that element — but the element records how fast an extent is changing and not which way , so a figure may reverse at a hinge and the element will not notice. This run measures each figure's arc element off the contour as length per unit turn, solves for the smooth figure that shares it, and draws the two side by side. Three outcomes appear, and telling them apart is the point. A smooth figure comes back as itself. A hinged figure usually cannot be fitted at all — no smooth figure has its arc element, and the residual says so out loud. And a figure built by reversing at hinges is fitted perfectly , to fourteen decimal places, by a different figure: the arrivals from the two are identical and nothing in them says which was sent. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the figure, recovered
The last step of the chain, done on the page. A figure walked at its own pace leaves its arc element — √(r²+r′²) through the turn — in the distribution of what arrives, and that much is recovered exactly. Solving back for the figure is a first-order equation, so it fixes the figure only up to one constant , and the constant is where the reader was standing. This run does the solving: from the arc element alone, with no knowledge of the figure, it fits the figure back in a Fourier basis — smooth and closed by construction — and draws it beside the one that was walked. It also draws what the same arc element admits behind the reader, since the equation does not care which sign r takes. That is the whole of the argument: the negative solution is not a rival answer, because a figure being read is a figure in front of the reader , and a reader reading the other one would have had nothing to read. And there is nothing else to exclude — two smooth figures in front of the reader that share an arc element are the same figure , since at the turn where two such figures differ most their extents must come out equal and opposite, which puts one of them behind. So what is drawn here is not the best candidate of several: among smooth figures it is the only one. Smoothness is a real condition and not a formality — the arc element records how fast an extent is changing and not which way, so a figure may reverse at a hinge — a kink where the extent turns abruptly, not the calibration this tool calls the corner — without the element noticing, and figures built by reversing at hinges share an arc element with the round one exactly. That assumption belongs to the account doing the solving, not to the relation. Replaces the page in one history frame.
what can be recovered
The whole question put to each figure at once: meet it, screen the arrivals, and draw back whatever they will give. Each figure appears in four cells. As held. Then met evenly in the turn , where the arrivals pass the screen — they are Cauchy, a frame comes back from them, and what the frame draws is a circle of radius one, the same one from every figure, because the division cancelled the figure before the arrivals were made. Then walked at the figure's own pace , where the arrivals FAIL the screen — and the failure is the point, since the departure is the figure showing through the sampling. From those arrivals the figure's arc element is recovered and drawn, beside the same quantity computed directly from the contour, so the two can be compared by eye. What is recovered is exact and is not the figure: it is √(r²+r′²), and solving back for r leaves one constant, which is where the reader was standing. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the outside streams
The screen has only ever judged streams the corpus made for it, and this run puts the whole library through it instead — every representable figure, met three ways , through the full battery : four shape ratios, the exchange taken about two centres, and the mean's refusal, with a finer quantile-function screen alongside whose noise floor is measured on honest draws before anything is called a catch. Met evenly every figure should pass, and any that fails is drawn. Walked at its own pace every figure whose radius varies should fail — the departure is the figure showing through the sampling — and any that slips past is drawn, because a varied figure whose own pace mimics evenness is exactly the edge case this run exists to find; the near-round figures pass honestly, a walk on a circle being even. On the ramp — the severely uneven schedule recorded as sitting inside the cheap statistic's pass band — the run measures whether that pass band is real on real figures, whether the rest of the battery catches what the one statistic misses, and how far the quiet walks while the numbers read clean. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the sweep, read three ways
A reader walking its relation meets the arrivals in order , and the sign servo was built for arrivals in no order at all — on an ordered sweep it converges, stably, to the wrong place, because placement is a whole-lap possession and a rule that forgets cannot hold one. This run puts three rules to the same ordered stream. Per arrival , the servo's trace parks off the corner with its manufactured unit inflated. Per lap , the same servo updated once a lap places the corner, because a lap consumed whole is a fair sample however it is ordered. And the lap rule places it in two laps with nothing shuffled anywhere: home and the horizon announce themselves in the register's own alphabet — a sign change among tiny sizes, a sign change at saturation — the rule counts the arrivals between them, and the arrival at half the count is the corner. Disorder was never the price; the price is one lap of counting between two marks the reader already owns. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the seed at zero
One question behind the ring, the seam, and the world: can this set of seeds be driven to zero at once? Below balance any testimony fits — a tree of readings witnesses anything, and four shared arrangements join any two accounts exactly, which is why four pins a seam and cannot check one. The wall stands at the first surplus statement: one added cycle, or the seam's fifth arrangement, and random testimony fails by fifteen orders while consistent testimony still fits to the arithmetic's floor. Testimony begins where seed statements outnumber the moduli they are statements about — the tree that cannot audit, the four that cannot check, and the quintuple no crowd convicts are one fact in three costumes. And one meter serves every instance: the visible share of a small lie is √(excess/statements), drawn here with each measured tooth beside its predicted one. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the stream bank
The evidence base's second stimulus family : streams in the sensor idiom — baselines at rest, transients, quantized channels, drifting walks, figures walked at their own pace, heavy-tailed noise that is not the family's — each drawn as signed rungs and put through the screen with a pre-registered expected verdict , asserted as a regression suite. Two rows carry the record's own findings in permanence: the walked oval is expected to PASS — the blind class, pinned, so that if its cell ever turns red the screen got sharper and the finding needs revisiting — and the ramp is expected to be caught by the exchange while the cheap statistic still reads inside its band. The widest shape ratio's band is floor-aware here, as in the ingestion harness, because a fixed 12% sits below that ratio's own sampling noise at short lengths. Everything on this page is synthetic and says so: the second family grows the evidence base, and the real-instrument gate stays exactly where it was. Replaces the page in one history frame.
sampling tests
What the arrivals carry depends on how the turn was met , and this run measures the difference on the library's own figures. Each is read twice. Stepped evenly in the turn , the readings come out Cauchy whatever the figure is — a shape statistic that stands at 3.078 for any Cauchy reads within a few hundredths of it for every one, so the figures are indistinguishable and nothing of them survives. Walked at a pace the figure sets — a constant speed along the contour, which advances the turn quickly where the figure stands far off and slowly where it stands near — the arrivals are no longer even in the turn, no longer Cauchy, and the departure is the figure showing through the sampling . The run also takes the walker's arrival density and returns the figure's arc element from it, against the truth computed directly, to show that the departure is a measurement and not merely a signature. What it cannot return is the figure itself: the arc element is √(r²+r′²), and solving back for r leaves one constant, which is where the reader was standing. Replaces the page in one history frame.
the recovered circle
What survives dividing, and what a census puts back. Each representable primitive is read the way a serial reader reads it — one arrival at a time, the described party stated in the describing party's terms — and dividing cancels the size of both , so what the readings carry is the turn and nothing else. Two things are then laid on the page beside the figure. First the arrivals , gathered into their distribution: they come out Cauchy for every figure, and the quartiles land at ±1 whether the figure was a circle, a star, a square or a bottle. Second the recovery : the readings are taken back up and the census applied — the resolved account's declaration that the two extents square to one — and what returns is drawn. The unit circle comes back from every one of them, and it is the same circle each time. Nothing is violated, because the radius that told the figures apart was never in the readings. The reconstruction is perfect and it is uninformative: it returns the census, not the figure. Replaces the page in one history frame.
two fisheyes on one array
One array of magnitudes, two fisheyes — each with its own focus, item width and pixel grain. Two Möbius charts of one line, drawn as two lenses. Screen positions do not transfer between them; cross ratios do , so a cross ratio against three shared landmarks is an address either view can send and the other can land on, with no shared scale — and three shared landmarks fix the whole map, so A predicts where every element lands in B. Drag, zoom, pick four, send an address, run the separation sweep, read the pyramid in rungs , see the context in octaves below each window, write to the array and watch both views change, or break B's chart and watch a fourth element's cross ratio catch it. The lab run The Projective Reader owes.
the ownership rule, shown
The rule laid out so it can be read across the page rather than taken on trust. One configuration of six arrangements is drawn three times — as held, restated by an affine account, and restated by a projective one — and three quantities are computed on it, one from each class the rule distinguishes. Every quantity is a ratio of disagreements , and each cell carries its value. Read a row left to right: the balanced, degree-zero quantity reads the same three times, because degree zero cancels the account's determinant and balance cancels its weight at each arrangement. The degree-zero but unbalanced quantity holds for the affine account, where every weight is one, and breaks the moment weights appear. The degree-one quantity breaks at once, since nothing cancels a determinant standing alone. The figures visibly move in all three rows; what differs is whether the number moves with them. Replaces the page in one history frame.
ownership tests
A rule for telling, in advance , which quantities belong to the pair and which belong to the page. Every quantity here is a ratio of products of disagreements — some D's above the line, some below — and two things about that ratio are counted before it is ever evaluated: its degree , the number of terms above minus the number below, and whether it is balanced , meaning every point appears exactly as often above as below. The claim under test is that those two counts decide everything. An account restating the figure multiplies every disagreement by its own determinant and divides it by a weight at each point, so degree zero cancels the determinant and balance cancels the weights — from which: balanced and degree zero should survive any account whatever; degree zero alone should survive a similarity and an affine map but not a projective one; and anything of nonzero degree should not even survive a change of scale. Expressions are generated at random in each class, evaluated on a configuration, and evaluated again after the figure is restated three ways. Each cell is a comb of what actually moved, one tooth per expression, from exact on the left to badly wrong on the right. A report, not a scene.
emoji sheet
A font nobody designed for this is the best corpus in the building. The shape sheet is 89 primitives someone wrote generators for; the keyboard sheet is 94 glyphs drawn by a type designer; the emoji font is hundreds of closed contours drawn by people solving a completely unrelated problem — no two by the same rule, full of things a generator would never produce, and every one of them a recognisable object. Traced from the system's own emoji face by alpha coverage , not by colour: a colour font ignores the fill it is handed and paints its own bitmap, so "where is it dark" is the wrong question and "where is it opaque" is the right one. Whatever the font here does not carry is measured and dropped, so you never get a grid of identical tofu boxes. It replaces the page; one undo brings the old one back.
keyboard sheet
Every key on the board as outlines, on one grid, in the font you pick — caps, lower case, the digit row, then the shifted punctuation — 94 in all. It is the shape sheet's argument applied to a better corpus: glyphs drawn by someone else, full of exactly what is hard — the counter inside an e , the join of an R , the spur on a j , two dozen sharp corners on a # . Every glyph is scaled by the SAME factor and sits on a shared baseline, so it reads as type: caps taller than x-height, descenders below the line. Each letter arrives as one group, its contours filled even-odd so counters are holes. It replaces the page; one undo brings the old one back.
brush
What a drag does to the contour. drag moves leaves directly; the rest are area operators applied through the brush ring, whose radius is the shape's smooth setting.
repair
The two repairs for a shape the current rung cannot hold: add resolution, or cut out the content that will not settle at any rung.
reconstruction
The open-aperture read is a Dirichlet sum, and that sum is a DFT: the leaves are the odd-node grid, so analysis is a radix-2 transform times the half-shift twiddle, and evaluating the interpolant at M points is the inverse transform of the zero-padded spectrum (TB companion §21). Same curve — agreement measured at ~10⁻¹³, nine orders below a pixel — at O(M log M) instead of O(N·M): 2–8× at the rungs where it is used (N ≥ 128; below that the direct sum is genuinely faster and is kept). The twiddle table is built from the leaf slopes by bisection and Möbius composition, with no trigonometric call (§21.4). Turn it off to A/B against the direct sum.
The window the aperture reads through is chosen per shape. A shape's own spectrum says how much of its band it is using; if it is using all of it — which is what the rung solver produces, since its job is to find the smallest sufficient rung — the tapered cardinal kernel is used. If it has a real guard band (a circle held at 512 leaves, anything refined past what it needs) the Fessler–Sutton min-max weights are used instead, which are optimal inside a band and need one to exist. Measured over 14 primitives: 3 qualify, 13× mean improvement, no shape made worse. The threshold is strict on purpose — relaxing it from 1e-6 to 1e-4 of the peak mode qualifies 13 of 14 and makes every one of them worse.
The bridge is exact at its atoms and may ring at a corner — that is the Dirichlet horn, and it is what the ringing overlay finds. Fejér is the other horn (§22): the same leaf readings under a triangular window, giving a positive kernel with operator norm exactly 1, which cannot ring for ANY continuous shape. It pays for that by no longer passing through its own leaves — the dots sit just off the line, approaching at O(1/N). A presentation only: the solve, the thumbnails and the export keep reading the bridge itself.
the dyadic lattice
§2.4 forces the radix: the cascade tiles only under g = 2, so the leaf lattice is N = 2^(d+1) and nothing else. Three separate dividends are collected on that one fact — the nesting of §5.3, the radix-2 transform of §21, and the reduced aperture lattice of §23.1, where the half-difference (φ−θ)/2 lands on p·π/Λ with Λ = 2MN/gcd(2N, M). The collapse to one small table needs gcd(2N, M) = min(2N, M), which is a statement about powers of two.

The slider does not enforce it. Off the lattice, both trig-free routes close at once — bandTable and fftReconUsable each open with !isPow2(N) || !isPow2(M) — and the windowed read falls back to evaluating the kernel per cell. Measured on the base-rule contour, cold: 12,540 trig calls at N = 128, and 2,486,988 at N = 300. The fallback is correct; it is simply outside the structure the theorem forces, and it pays for that.
—
observer aperture
Reconstruct each point from only the leaves within a local window (raised-cosine taper), instead of the full unbounded sum. 1.00 = full (the default, identical to no windowing). A leaf's far-field influence falls as ~1/N and the window truncates it to zero — an observable instrument, not a drawing aid. Exact at the leaves at any setting; it does not reduce corner ringing.
